institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: As a person who loved being outside, Svalbard provided an exciting place to combine geological education combined with lots of fieldwork in very hard and unexplored conditions and sites.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:

questions.answer: Upon arrival, all the information we gathered was rather straightforward, so I didn't experience a lot of problem getting to know the systems and operations.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Since Longyearbyen in Svalbard is quite a small city, there is not a lot of activities outside of hiking, some sports, fitness, and social gatherings in the evening. But a lot of time is spent together with your fellow students in the kitchen, watching movies, partying, playing games, etc. But not a lot of activities outside that.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The people at UNIS, was very helpful when it came to questions related to different stuff like exams, like filling out paper, but generally I didn't need that much help, so I can't really answer this question fully.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Since you can't directly apply to UNIS or if you want to get Erasmus, it's kind of a long process to get up there. You need to fill out a lot of documents and papers. It's worth it, but it can easily scare a lot of people away.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a very fun, learningful, and exciting exchange to Svalbard.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses sound very much like an introduction course, so it's from what I could learn from the teachers. The course just didn't only need, or couldn't only be attended by people who have already studied geology, but also people from other backgrounds. That's why it was pretty introductory. So I wouldn't say the level was very high, but I think it was pretty good. I have had experience with more difficult courses here in Copenhagen, but it was fun up there.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The education at Svalbard was very much dominated by fieldwork. We spent many hours and many days out doing fieldwork at different sites, where we combined with theory from the classroom, we went out to the location and saw them on the actual location and with our own eyes. My education in Copenhagen also, we had fieldwork included in it, but not as much and under different conditions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: AG214 (The Geological evolution of Svalbard) and Ag215 (Arctic Landforms and Processes)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Since there's only two courses for Arctic Geology every semester, so it's difficult for me to tell about the other courses since I haven't had them. But I would definitely recommend the two I had while I was up there.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Due to the conditions that the university was placed in and the location, there wasn't a lot of activities related to the university, but there were some small football and other social events in the town, but which was not related to the university.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Due to the conditions that the university was placed in and the location, there wasn't a lot of activities related to the university, but there were some small football and other social events in the town, but which was not related to the university.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Since it's a very small town and there's not a lot of activities going on, but of course hiking around the area is really beautiful. There's also a sports center where you can play football, you can go to the gym, swimming, badminton, etc. So I would recommend that. And there's also some quiz evenings where you battle against other groups for a small prize.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: It very much depends on how much they prioritize their lessons or their homework. But else, go on a hike with your fellow students. Maybe go play football in the sports center or go do other activities. But there's not a lot, so you need to be pretty creative with what you think of doing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Since it is part of Norway, the culture was very similar to Danish culture. That's why I didn't require a lot of getting used to their culture. But it is a small city that I lived in, so of course it is a bit more close neighborhood. So you start learning people relatively, or you start talking with people relatively quickly compared to in a big city.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't only stay in your rooms, go out and join social activities such as playing football, or going to the quiz evening, or playing board games at the church. But you need to go outside your housing area because nothing really happens there.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No big cultural differences

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Outdoor culture

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: A lover of the outside, be ready for hard conditions, small and tight and social classes.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nope

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I love the mixture of theoretical knowledge that we gained in the classroom, and then we saw and looked at the same theory, but in practice in the actual locations. But I also enjoyed the very laid-back attitude of a lot of the teachers that we have. It was very down-to-earth, and I think that it was a very good way of them, in a positive way, bonding to the class, that we, in many ways, respected them more, since they were very down-to-earth, and they could laugh with us, they could joke around with us, but also they are very knowledgeable, and we learned a lot of things from them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: All the paperwork that was needed to be filled out prior to me leaving Denmark

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.answer: Yes
